instructions: Cut each block of halloumi lengthwise into 1/2 inch slices and pat them dry with paper towels. Slice the tomatoes 1/2 inch thick.
In a shallow bowl, stir the 2 tbsp cornstarch together with the 1/2 tsp black pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tomato slices in one layer and sprinkle on the 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 1 minute on each side, until they have brown spots. Transfer them to a platter.
Turn the heat to medium. Press half the halloumi slices into the cornstarch to coat both sides and shake off the extra.
Add 1 1/2 tbsp of the remaining oil to the skillet, then the coated halloumi. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes on each side, until golden. Transfer it to the platter next to the tomatoes.
Coat the rest of the halloumi and cook it the same way in the last 1 1/2 tbsp oil.
Halve the lemon and squeeze it over the halloumi. Put the red pepper flakes in a small bowl for anyone who wants heat.
Serve right away with the tomatoes. Halloumi turns chewy as it cools.
method_notes: Joudie Kalla's halloumi meshwi, via Tara's Multicultural Table, is the lead: slices dredged in a seasoned dusting, pan-fried 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden and finished with lemon, served at once. Her dusting is flour with red pepper flakes, so cornstarch stands in for the flour to keep it gluten-free and the pepper flakes move to the table. The seared tomato comes from a Gulf News grilled halloumi with tomato. The list's cucumber isn't in any version read, so it's left out. No version had a rating, so the lead is a fallback and RecipeTin Eats has no halloumi dish.
